$comment: Canonical screen/navigation map. Built from iOS's Support/AppRoute.swift + ContentView.swift, Android's ui/ProsaryApp.kt NavHost, and Windows's Navigation/Router.cs usage across Views/*.xaml.cs. Parameter names/types here are the logical contract every platform's own route/query-param/navigation-parameter mechanism should carry, not literal syntax. Keep in sync whenever a screen or its parameters change on any platform — see README.md in this directory.

home.purpose: One card per devotion — the Rosary first, then every discovered generic (bundle-driven) devotion in pack-load order (title/accent/icon read from each bundle's own manifest — see customDevotionFlow), then the Jesus Prayer last — each showing that devotion's default favorite; plus a "Today" section (the day's feast per the Holy Land Latin calendar and the Pope's monthly prayer intention, from the bundled Shared/data datasets — rows hide when the datasets have no entry); plus My Favorites/Settings/About. The Rosary card opens the preset picker (default preset up top, then Pray-any-Rosary ad-hoc quick setup with save-as-preset, then the remaining presets) rather than launching a session directly.

favorites.purpose: Saved favorites: full card lists with Pray/Edit/Delete/Set-Default and an Add-new button for the two configurable kinds (Rosary, Jesus Prayer), plus one star-row per generic devotion in pack-load order (favorite toggle + the generic-devotion editor: schema-driven rows for the bundle's options.json options above the reminders section), an Import Devotion Bundle button (file picker -> PrayerPackStore.installPack), and a remove affordance on user-imported rows.

favoriteEditor.purpose: Create or edit a favorite of any kind; kind-specific sections shown conditionally.

prayerId.description: Editing an existing favorite. Null when creating new.

newFavoriteKind.description: Seeds a brand-new favorite's kind when prayerId is null. iOS passes the whole ad-hoc Prayer object directly instead (sheet(item:)); Android/Windows thread this + prayerId as separate params since neither has an iOS-sheet-style whole-object-across-navigation mechanism.

rosaryFlow.purpose: The Rosary prayer flow — season bar, progress, bead track, mystery image/text, Back/Next footer.

prayerId.description: Favorite to pray; null falls back to the default Rosary favorite.

reachedVia.iOS: The generic prayer(id) route -> PrayerDispatchView resolves the Prayer and picks the flow by kind.
reachedVia.android: The generic prayer/{id} route -> PrayerDispatchScreen, same dispatch-by-kind pattern.
reachedVia.windows: Routed to directly by name (RosaryPrayerPage) — Home/Favorites already hold the full Prayer in memory, so Windows skips the generic-dispatcher indirection entirely (see ARCHITECTURE.md, "Skip iOS's PrayerDispatchView indirection").

customDevotionFlow.purpose: The single flow for every generic (bundle-driven) devotion (PrayerKind.custom): Angelus, Stations of the Cross, Franciscan Crown, Seven Sorrows, Divine Mercy Chaplet, Trisagion. Steps/title/season color are entirely data-driven from the bundle's devotion.json/manifest.json — see ARCHITECTURE.md's "Content bundles" section. A decade/bead-structured ("rosary" type) devotion renders the same bead track as rosaryFlow (shown whenever any built step carries a decadeIndex; hasClosingCross from the definition); flat ("steps" type) devotions get a plain progress bar. Has its own favorite-star toggle since it can be launched with no saved favorite at all. Adding a new generic devotion needs no new screen, just a new bundle. Bundles declaring variants (alternate step-sets) additionally get a toolbar variant menu that rebuilds the session on switch and persists Prayer.variantId to the matching favorite. When the bundle ships a narrated recording matching the session's language and variant (audio.json), a compact transport bar appears above the footer — chapter skip / play-pause / seekable timeline / current chapter title. The chapters' advisory stepIndex hints drive the step while playing, manual Back/Next re-aligns the recording to the chapter narrating the new step, and the timer auto-advance stands down during playback. Multi-day (days-type) bundles add a calendar toolbar menu listing every day (period-prefixed for Montfort-style groupings); the session prays the favorite's saved dayIndex, switching persists it, and finishing a day advances it (clamped to the last).

devotionId.description: The bundle id (e.g. "angelus") to load — always required, even when a favorite exists, since PrayerKind.custom alone doesn't say which devotion to load.

prayerId.description: Launched from a saved favorite. Null when launched from Home with no favorite saved yet for this devotionId — falls back to the app's default language (generic devotions have no per-favorite options).

reachedVia.iOS: The generic prayer(id) route -> PrayerDispatchView resolves the Prayer and picks CustomDevotionFlowView by kind (reading devotionId from Prayer.customDevotionId); a fresh (no-favorite) launch uses AppRoute.custom(devotionId:) instead.
reachedVia.android: The generic prayer/{id} route -> PrayerDispatchScreen, same dispatch-by-kind pattern; a fresh launch uses the custom/{devotionId} route.
reachedVia.windows: Routed to directly by name (CustomDevotionFlowPage) via CustomDevotionFlowParams(prayerId, bundleId) — Home/Favorites already know the bundle id at the call site, so Windows skips the generic-dispatcher indirection entirely, same as rosaryFlow.

sources.note: Windows' page carries its own copy of RosaryPrayerPage's bead-track XAML (Visibility-bound to ShowsBeadTrack), absorbed from the deleted FranciscanCrownFlowPage — that platform has no shared bead-track control.

jesusPrayerSetup.purpose: Repetition-count picker (33/66/99/Custom/Unbounded) before starting a fresh Jesus Prayer session.

jesusPrayerFlow.purpose: The Jesus Prayer flow — single fixed line + repetition counter, no engine. Own favorite-star toggle, same reason as angelusFlow.

prayerId.description: Launched from a saved favorite — its own target overrides target, and its language is used.

target.description: Set when launched fresh from jesusPrayerSetup (no favorite yet).

jesusPrayerFlow.navigationNote: Finish (pop-to-Home) and the back arrow (pop-one-level, back to Setup) are deliberately distinct commands — see ARCHITECTURE.md and JesusPrayerViewModel's class doc.

about.purpose: Attribution: typefaces, mystery/other image sources, Scripture sources. Static content.

sources.iOS: Views/About/AboutView.swift (Mac: app-menu-only, own window; iPhone/iPad: linked from Home)

settings.purpose: App-wide preferences: the default prayer language (+ rite when the language has more than one), auto-advance, haptics (iOS), the Today row's liturgical calendar (a picker over Shared/data/calendars.json's registry, persisted as feastCalendarId beside defaultLanguageCode, hidden if the registry ships a single calendar), downloads management, and links.

sources.iOS: Views/Settings/SettingsView.swift (macOS Settings scene, Cmd+,; iOS has no in-app equivalent — the system Settings app via Settings.bundle/Root.plist instead)
sources.android: ui/settings/SettingsScreen.kt (Android has no external settings surface to extend, unlike iOS)

rosaryPresetPicker.purpose: Home -> Rosary: the default preset (one tap to pray), a Pray-any-Rosary quick setup (iOS/Android embed the full Rosary options editor seeded from the default preset; Windows exposes the mystery selection inline and inherits the rest from the default preset — a deliberate, documented divergence), with save-as-preset (never stealing the default slot unless it's the first preset), then the remaining presets. Preset management stays in Favorites (a Manage action links there). Ad-hoc sessions are unsaved: iOS routes a Prayer value (AppRoute.rosaryQuickPray), Android rides a holder object (Compose routes are strings), Windows passes the Prayer as the navigation parameter.

repositoryBrowser.purpose: The in-app browser for prayers.prosary.app: fetches the versioned /index.json catalog, filters by search text and tag, and installs a bundle through the same installPack pipeline as a manual file import (star row, 'Repository' tag, remove affordance all identical). Downloads go through the catalog's same-origin /api/download/<id> path so server-side counting works.
repositoryBrowser.navigation: The Browse tab (primary), plus the Favorites screen's 'Get Community Devotions…' row (sheet on iOS).

sources.android: ui/favorites/RepositoryBrowserScreen.kt (route favorites/repository) + content/repository/RepositoryClient.kt (the app's first and only INTERNET-permission feature)

tabShell.purpose: The app's top-level navigation: four sections — Pray (Home), Browse (the prayers.prosary.app catalog), Categories (devotions grouped by manifest tags), Search (local + community). Bottom tab bar on phones; sidebar on desktop (iOS 18/macOS 15 sidebarAdaptable, Android NavigationRail at >=840dp, WinUI NavigationView pane). Inner screens (flows, editors) hide the tab chrome on Android; each iOS tab owns its own NavigationStack; Windows resets the frame back stack on section switch so sections feel like tabs.

categories.purpose: View prayers by category: every launchable devotion (Rosary, loaded bundles, Jesus Prayer) grouped by its manifest tags via the shared DevotionDirectory; a devotion appears under each of its tags, untagged ones under 'Other'.

search.purpose: One search across everything prayable: local devotions (opened in place, title/tag match) and the prayers.prosary.app catalog (installed in place); the repository half degrades silently offline.

basicPrayers.purpose: The basic prayers on their own, outside any devotion (Erez, 2026-08-07): Sign of the Cross, Our Father, Hail Mary, Glory Be, the Creed (2026-08-08 — the shared tables' Apostles', which the Mission of St. Gamaliel's overlay replaces with the Nicene), and the Trisagion's Holy God — a fixed BasicPrayerCatalog naming keys, never text, so each row and its prayer resolve in the prayer language through the same chains the flows use, rites included (Erez's rite reads קדישת over his own acclamation). The list is reorderable (Erez, 2026-08-08) via BasicPrayersOrder, the HomeOrder pattern: a persisted id list, catalog order for ids it doesn't name. Reached from a fixed, non-pinnable row below the Pray cards. Each prayer opens as a single bounded step in the shared flow chrome with Finish as its only action.

parameters.prayerId: BasicPrayerCatalog id ("hailMary") — the single-prayer flow only.
